page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. There is no bundled local storage or GPU acceleration included with this instance type.

Benchmark results indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core processing is a relative bottleneck, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the weak and poor categories respectively. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as demonstrated by average ratings in Geekbench multi-core, Passmark CPU, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks consistently register average performance, though Passmark memory scores are comparatively weak.

The instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.se1.4xlarge offers a dense memory allocation relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand high single-core CPU performance. It is well-suited for workloads such as database operations, Redis caching, static web serving, and moderate multi-threaded processing tasks, while being less optimal for single-threaded applications or heavy LLM inference.
